canonical.title: A weekend in Valence: what to do around the Michelin dinner

parent.title: A weekend in Valence, Drôme — anchored on a Michelin dinner

siblings.title: Michelin 2 and 3-star restaurants in Valence
siblings.summary: Restaurant Pic (3 stars, Anne-Sophie Pic) is Valence's sole multi-star Michelin table; two 1-star options in the centre.

siblings.title: IT conferences and tech events in Valence
siblings.summary: No large international IT conferences; local scene runs through French Tech Alpes Valence-Romans.

sources.title: Le Pendentif — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: Free 1548 Renaissance funerary monument, one of France's first listed historic monuments (1840).

sources.title: Maison des Têtes de Valence — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Built 1528–1532, Gothic-to-Renaissance transition, facade carved with allegorical heads.

sources.title: Maison des Têtes — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: Courtyard free, no booking required.

sources.title: Musée de Valence
sources.claim: Wed–Sun 10–12:30 / 14–18 (Jul–Aug 10–18), closed Mon & Tue.

sources.title: Musée de Valence – admission
sources.claim: €9/€7 until 21 Jun 2026, €6/€4 from 22 Jun.

sources.title: Parc Jouvet — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: 7 ha, Jardin Remarquable since 2006, inaugurated 1905.

sources.title: Kiosque Peynet — Wikipedia
sources.claim: 1890 bandstand by Poitoux, inspired Peynet's 'Amoureux' (1942), MH 1982.

sources.title: Champ de Mars — Valence.fr
sources.claim: 3 ha esplanade created 1773, panoramic view of Château de Crussol.

sources.title: Vieux Valence — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Medieval côtes: Saint-Martin, Saint-Estève, Sainte-Ursule, des Chapeliers, de la Voûte.

sources.title: Hiking the Hermitage hillside — Ardèche Hermitage
sources.claim: Signposted trail 'Sur les Pas de Gambert, en Hermitage' up through vineyards.

sources.title: Tain top 6 ideas — Ardèche Hermitage
sources.claim: 45 min from Taurobole sq. to Chapelle Saint-Christophe, or 10 min from Pierre Aiguille belvedere.

sources.title: Marc Seguin Bridge — Structurae
sources.claim: Oldest suspension bridge in France still in service (1847–49).

sources.title: Marc Seguin — Linda Hall Library
sources.claim: The Seguin brothers built the world's first wire-cable suspension bridge here in 1825.

sources.title: Château-Musée de Tournon — Ardèche Hermitage
sources.claim: Daily 18 Mar–1 Nov 2026; May–June afternoons only 14–18. €5/€4.

sources.title: Train de l'Ardèche
sources.claim: Steam train into Gorges du Doux; departs Tournon 10:15, returns 17:00.

sources.title: Paul Jaboulet Aîné — Vineum
sources.claim: Three tasting formats: by-the-glass, paired chef menu, guided session.

sources.title: M. Chapoutier tasting cellar
sources.claim: Walk-in OK, Mon PM–Sat 10–12 / 14–18.

sources.title: Cave de Tain
sources.claim: 45-min visit + 5 wines €15/pp. Daily May–Aug 10:30 & 15:30 (FR), 14:30 (EN). Book required.

sources.title: Gang of Mauves — The Buyer
sources.claim: Gonon, Chave, Coursodon, Gripa — cult Saint-Joseph producers; almost never walk-in.

sources.title: Domaine du Colombier
sources.claim: Mercurol, Apr–Oct daily 9:30–12:30 / 14:30–19. Walk-in.

sources.title: Château de Crussol loop — AllTrails
sources.claim: ~4.8 km, ~210 m gain, 1.5–2 h moderate hike.

sources.title: Château de Crussol — Ardèche Guide
sources.claim: 20 min from castle car park, 40 min from tourist office.

sources.title: Château de Crussol — Guide to Europe
sources.claim: Best months April–June and September–October; bring water.

sources.title: Carbone Zéro — ViaRhôna
sources.claim: 24 rue Denis Papin, next to Valence gare, classic and e-bikes, Accueil Vélo certified.

sources.title: ViaRhôna Tain→Valence — Ardèche Guide
sources.claim: ~19 km stabilised greenway through Hermitage vineyards.

sources.title: Suisse de Valence — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: Soldier-shaped shortbread, created 1799 to honour Swiss Guards who accompanied Pope Pius VI's body.

sources.title: Maison Nivon — Suisse
sources.claim: Founded 1856 by Félix Henry Léon Nivon; 250g ≈ €8.50.

sources.title: Ravioles du Dauphiné — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: Label Rouge + IGP since 2009, production restricted to Romans–Saint-Marcellin.

sources.title: La Ravioline — Gault&Millau
sources.claim: 18 rue Dauphine, market bistro built around ravioles, chef Alexandre from Romans.

sources.title: Pogne de Romans — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: Crown brioche, orange blossom, medieval Easter origin.

sources.title: Maison Pascalis — Pogne de Romans
sources.claim: Founded Bourg-de-Péage 1892, four generations.

sources.title: Picodon AOP
sources.claim: Small firm raw-goat cheese AOP since 1983; name from Provençal picaoudou.

sources.title: Saturday Market — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: Place des Clercs, 7am–2pm year-round, ~100 stalls.

sources.title: Musée international de la Chaussure
sources.claim: 16,500 pieces spanning 4,000 years in a former Visitation convent.

sources.title: Marques Avenue Romans — Valence Romans Tourisme
sources.claim: 80+ outlet boutiques, 30% off year-round, up to 70% in sales.

sources.title: Cité de la Raviole — free tasting
sources.claim: Free factory visit with tasting at Mère Maury, Mours-Saint-Eusèbe.

sources.title: Tour de Crest
sources.claim: Tallest medieval keep in France at 52 m; open daily 10–19 May–Sept.

sources.title: Tour de Crest — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Built 13th c., state prison 17th–mid 19th c.

sources.title: Château de Grignan — Année Sévigné 2026
sources.claim: 2026 marks 400th anniversary of Madame de Sévigné's birth; full event programme.

sources.title: Mirmande — Plus Beaux Villages
sources.claim: Stone hilltop village, revived by cubist André Lhote's summer school.

sources.title: Forêt de Saoû closure
sources.claim: Partial closure 15 May–15 July to protect chamois during calving.

sources.title: Lavender season — Travel France Bucket List
sources.claim: In early June lavender fields are still green.

sources.title: Lavender flowering — Routes Lavande
sources.claim: Drôme provençale lavandin starts mid-June in the plain, mid-July at altitude.

sources.title: Tain → Valence train times — Trainline
sources.claim: ~27 trains/day, ~10 min journey.

sources.title: Musée de Valence hours
sources.claim: Wed–Sun 10–12 / 14–18; closed Monday AND Tuesday.

sources.title: Maison Pic — Relais & Châteaux
sources.claim: Anne-Sophie Pic's hotel; 15-min walk from Champ de Mars.

sources.title: Q-Park Champ de Mars
sources.claim: 842 spaces, 24/7, next to Peynet kiosk and museum.
